name: Terrestrial Ecology Scheduler, Predator Territories & Cross-Biome Population Persistence
design_rules: terrestrial populations persist by biome across world days
predator territories constrain local predator density
hunting requires prey to exist in the same or linked shoreline habitat
cross-biome dispersal redistributes individuals without creating population
wetland linkage increases shoreline hunting opportunities
prey scarcity reduces successful hunting and encourages dispersal
territory competition may force excess predators into neighboring biomes
terrestrial ecology never uses emissive or glow feedback
